scams.name: The Scippatori Scooter Bag & Watch Snatch
scams.description: Two men on a scooter or motorcycle ride up alongside a pedestrian — often a tourist with a visible handbag or luxury watch — the passenger rips the bag or watch off in one motion and they vanish into the vicoli. A Napolitoday cronaca report documents a tourist aggredito da due ragazzi in scooter on Corso Arnaldo Lucci losing his Rolex, with the pair fleeing into the rione delle Case Nuove. On November 15, 2024, Naples Polizia and Spanish police arrested five Naples-linked suspects (ages 18–52, including one woman who spotted victims) for a Spain-wide Rolex-robbery ring that stole a €50,000 Rolex from a British tourist in Puerto Banús — the same moped MO they use at home. A July 2025 edizionecaserta blitz in the Casertano indicted 22 and arrested 9 for Rolex thefts targeting wealthy tourists, with €374,000 in watches recovered.
scams.avoidance: Do not wear a visible luxury watch, chain, or designer bag in Naples — wear a cheap watch and leave the Rolex in the hotel safe. Carry handbags on the inside (wall side) shoulder, with the strap crossbody, not on the street side. Never walk close to the curb; keep one meter between you and any passing scooter. If you hear an approaching scooter slow behind you, stop, face it, and put your hand firmly on your bag. If a bag or watch is snatched, do not chase — call 112 and report to the Polizia di Stato at Questura di Napoli, Via Medina 75.
scams.location: Corso Arnaldo Lucci (near Napoli Centrale), Via Toledo, Via Partenope / Lungomare, Mergellina, Chiaia, Piazza dei Martiri, Corso Umberto

scams.name: Napoli Centrale & Piazza Garibaldi Pickpocket Rings
scams.description: Piazza Garibaldi and the Napoli Centrale concourse are the densest pickpocket zone in southern Italy, with coordinated crews working the arrivals board, metro entrance, and platform approaches. A Napolitoday investigation quotes citizens that the zone is 'nelle mani dei borseggiatori' — 'Nel mirino soprattutto i turisti, bersagli facili di un sistema criminale che sfrutta il caos e la confusione dell'area.' An October 2024 r/ItalyTravel firsthand post documents a 69-year-old woman chasing down a late-20s thief who lifted a lilac backpack off her rolling suitcase while she sat under the departures board around 22:00 waiting for a night train to Palermo — the husband spotted the lift from the corner of his eye. A 2023 r/solotravel post with 1,300 upvotes documents a female tourist having her phone lifted from her pocket on a crowded sidewalk outside the station in the middle of the day — she chased and screamed until the thief dropped it. A separate Napolitoday report documents a German tourist pickpocketed on Metro Linea 1, with the thief caught and arrested for furto aggravato.
scams.avoidance: Treat the 500 meters around Piazza Garibaldi like Rome Termini or a Bangkok night market. Wear a crossbody bag with zippers facing your body, zipper-pinned or locked. Move luggage continuously — never set a backpack on top of a roller and look away. Exit to the taxi rank via the main station atrium, not the side exits onto Corso Novara or Piazza Principe Umberto. If you're pickpocketed, yell 'ladro!' loudly — the r/solotravel 1,300-score story confirms yelling recovers the item because thieves flee attention.
scams.location: Napoli Centrale station concourse, Piazza Garibaldi, Corso Umberto, Corso Garibaldi, Metro Linea 1 and Circumvesuviana platforms, Piazza Principe Umberto

scams.name: The Tre Campanelle (Three-Bells) Shell Game
scams.description: A portable cardboard stand on Piazza Garibaldi runs the classic tre campanelle shell game — three shiny bells and a hidden ball. Shills posing as tourists 'win' to lure you in; the conductor palms the ball the whole time; lookouts warn of approaching police. In September 2024 the Carabinieri Compagnia Stella arrested three men running the game at Piazza Garibaldi and seized the stand after 'numerose segnalazioni' from citizens and tourists (per Cronache della Campania and Il Mattino's 'giro di vite contro truffatori e banchetti spenna-turisti'). Fanpage's headline put the lifespan of the con starkly: 'dopo 50 anni possibile che ci caschino ancora?' A 2024 Ottopagine Napoli report documents the scam still mietendo vittime on the same piazza. Tourists typically lose €100–€500 in a single session before realizing every 'winning' bet was a shill and every 'losing' bet was themselves.
scams.avoidance: If you see a cardboard table with three cups, three bells, or three shells on Piazza Garibaldi, Via Toledo, or any piazza crowd, walk away — it is never not a scam, and you cannot win. Do not stop to watch 'just to see if it's fair' — the crowd around the stand contains lookouts who mark you as interested and then target you for pickpocketing even if you don't bet. Do not accept 'free try' offers. If you've already lost money, report at the Polizia Municipale office in Napoli Centrale — the Comune Stella Carabinieri have an active anti-campanelle operation.
scams.location: Piazza Garibaldi (especially the pedestrian side near Napoli Centrale), Corso Umberto, Piazza Dante, Via Toledo crowd chokepoints

scams.name: The Circumvesuviana (Pompeii-Bound) Pickpocket Gang
scams.description: The Circumvesuviana commuter rail — the crowded, un-air-conditioned line that carries tourists from Napoli Porta Nolana / Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi, Ercolano, and Sorrento — is worked by an identified pickpocket crew. A Napolitoday cronaca report, 'Stanata la banda di borseggiatori della Circumvesuviana,' documents the arrest of a crew caught mid-lift: 'nel corso del viaggio, uno degli indagati avrebbe tentato il borseggio del portafogli di un turista, scena a cui aveva assistito un altro agente' in plainclothes. The train is 'one of Italy's worst commuter rail lines by punctuality' (a local commenter on r/ItalyTravel) and the carriages on the Pompei-bound and Sorrento-bound runs are packed standing-room-only at peak tourist hours, making it trivial to hand off wallets between accomplices. A separate Napolitoday report documents pickpocket arrests on Metro Linea 1 with a German tourist as the victim.
scams.avoidance: Consider the Campania Express (€15 extra, reserved seats, fewer stops) for Pompei and Sorrento during peak summer hours — its reserved seating removes the standing crush where the theft happens. On the standard Circumvesuviana, never board with valuables in outer backpack pockets or back trouser pockets. Wear a money belt under clothing. Sit rather than stand whenever possible; if you must stand, keep your back to a wall or carriage end. Watch for the classic distraction combo: someone 'falling' or 'arguing' while another crew member works pockets behind you.
scams.location: Circumvesuviana line — Napoli Porta Nolana, Napoli Piazza Garibaldi, Ercolano Scavi, Pompei Scavi Villa dei Misteri, Sorrento

scams.name: The Capodichino Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Capodichino airport drivers refuse the posted tariffa predeterminata, switch the meter to a long-distance tariff, or quote double the fixed rate hoping tourists don't know it. The 2024–2025 Comune di Napoli fixed fares are €21 airport → Piazza Garibaldi/Stazione Centrale, €24 airport → Molo Beverello/Piazza Municipio, and €28.50 airport → Via Partenope / Mergellina — all inclusive of luggage, night, holiday, and airport supplements (per the official Comune di Napoli 'tariffe predeterminate' schedule and Il Mattino's reporting). On r/napoli, a tourist reports a driver demanding €55 from Stazione Centrale to the ferry port — a 4-km trip that should be €10–15 on the meter. A 2024 r/napoli thread documents even the FreeNow app being gamed: an estimated €15.38 ride was edited post-drop to €28.01; FreeNow refunded after a complaint. An Il Mattino report documents a driver who not only overcharged a Naples consigliere comunale (Paipais) but handed him counterfeit change. The Il Mattino 'sfida dei B&B ai tassisti senza regole' feature describes Naples B&Bs distributing a vademecum telling guests to photograph the driver's license number on the dashboard.
scams.avoidance: Before closing the door, say 'tariffa predeterminata per Piazza Garibaldi, ventuno euro' (or the relevant destination) — the driver is legally required to accept the fixed fare and provide a receipt with the route and amount before departure. Use only the official white taxis at the signed Capodichino rank; refuse all 'taxi?' offers inside arrivals. Photograph the license number (codice identificativo taxi) on the rear of the vehicle before you get in. Prefer the Alibus shuttle (€5, ~20 minutes to Piazza Garibaldi/Molo Beverello, buy at newsagent) for airport transfers. For in-city rides, use FreeNow or NoxNo and check the final fare against the app estimate; dispute via in-app support if edited. Never accept 'credit-card-broken' redirects to an ATM.
scams.location: Capodichino airport taxi rank, Napoli Centrale rank, Piazza Municipio / Beverello port rank, hotel-door hails in Chiaia and Santa Lucia

scams.name: The Via Toledo "Salt & Corno" Gift Scam
scams.description: Operators work Via Toledo and Spaccanapoli carrying a paper bag of salt and a handful of small red cornicelli (lucky-horn charms). They engage tourists in friendly chat, press a corno into your hand as a 'gift,' then demand €10–€50 for the salt-sprinkling 'blessing' or the trinket itself — and turn aggressive if refused. A July 2025 r/napoli post with 121 upvotes, 'Turisti, fate attenzione!', from a local warns: 'Via Toledo è invasa da truffatori. Li riconosci perché hanno in mano un pacco di sale e dei piccoli corni rossi… Inizieranno a chiacchierare con voi e poi vi assilleranno per ricevere dei soldi. Tirate dritto e non fermatevi. Sono arroganti e aggressivi.' A top comment confirms the mechanism: 'cercano di disidratarti con il sale e poi ti vendono l'acqua a peso d'oro' (jokingly) — but the core reported pattern is the trinket press plus pressure. It is the Naples twin of Rome's 'friendship bracelet' scam and operates on the same instinct-reflex: once the charm is in your hand, the aggressor treats it as yours and demands payment.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets when any stranger on Via Toledo or in the Centro Storico approaches with anything in their hands — do not open your palm, do not reach for anything. If something is pressed into your hand, drop it on the ground immediately and walk away; the aggressor will pick it up rather than lose it. Reply to any 'un regalo!' or 'per te, gratis!' approach with a firm 'no, grazie' and keep moving. Do not stop to be photographed, hugged, or 'blessed' by street performers or anyone not connected to a licensed, signage-clear business. Report persistent aggressors to the Polizia Municipale station on Via Toledo.
scams.location: Via Toledo (entire length), Spaccanapoli / Via dei Tribunali, Piazza del Plebiscito, Galleria Umberto I, Piazza Dante

scams.name: The Centro Storico Tourist-Menu & Coperto Trap
scams.description: Restaurants clustered on Spaccanapoli, Via dei Tribunali, Via San Gregorio Armeno, and the lower Quartieri Spagnoli add high coperto charges (often €2–€4 per head), automatic 10–15% servizio, unrequested pane/acqua/limoncello 'gifts' billed on the check, and seafood or steak priced 'al etto' that arrives at 4–6 times the expected portion. Even famous venues like Gino Sorbillo's pizzerias charge a coperto and a servizio (one documented receipt lists 'Servizio 10% €1.33' plus coperto), which is legal if posted on the menu but often surprises tourists who expected the Roman convention. The Il Mattino interview with Naples Prefect Antonio De Iesu warns that 'i turisti truffati devono rivolgersi ai vigili urbani' (tourists who've been overcharged should report to the municipal police). A 2024 r/napoli FAQ names Quartieri Spagnoli as a 'sketchy area now turned tourist nightlife hot spot' — meaning the restaurant density there is high and uneven.
scams.avoidance: Before sitting down, photograph the full posted menu (Italian law requires prices to be displayed outside). Ask 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?' at the moment you sit — get the numbers verbally, not at the bill. For fish or steak priced 'al etto' (per 100g), ask the waiter to weigh it and confirm the total before it's cooked. Walk 3–5 minutes off the main tourist arteries — Vomero, Sanità, Chiaia back-streets, and Porta Capuana typically have local prices. Use Google Maps sorted by Italian reviews, Most Recent; if a venue's Italian rating is 4.5+ and English rating is 3.5, it's usually authentic (reversed, it's usually a trap). Never accept 'gift' limoncello, coffee, or antipasti without asking 'è compreso?' first.
scams.location: Spaccanapoli, Via dei Tribunali, Via San Gregorio Armeno, Quartieri Spagnoli, Piazza Bellini, Via Toledo restaurant alcoves

scams.name: The Fantasma (Ghost) Apartment Rental Scam
scams.description: Fraudulent 'hosts' post apartments on Airbnb, Booking, and especially Facebook Marketplace / Subito.it, collect deposits off-platform, and vanish before check-in — the address is real but the flat isn't theirs, or the address doesn't exist at all. Il Mattino's 'Ischia case vacanze fantasma' report documents a 38-year-old from Marano arrested by carabinieri for running a web-based maxi-truffa of affittanze fasulle to tourists. A separate Il Mattino Salerno report documents a €500 ghost-rental sting in Battipaglia; the Roccaraso snow-holiday report documents eight young people from Castellammare losing €1,500 to a nonexistent casa in via Pedemontana. An August 2025 ANSA Campania report warns specifically of case vacanze scams in Cilento as tourist demand spikes: 'La domanda turistica nel Cilento è in forte crescita e questo, purtroppo, attira anche malintenzionati.' The Il Mattino Booking report documents London-pattern cases where scammers list somebody else's real house using photos from another city entirely.
scams.avoidance: Book only on Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, or another pay-through-platform service — never wire a deposit or pay by bank transfer for a Naples rental you haven't entered. Check the listing address on Google Street View before you arrive; confirm the building matches the photos. If the host asks you to move to WhatsApp or email for 'a better deal,' refuse and keep all communication in the platform chat (this preserves your refund rights). Reverse-image-search the listing photos — if they appear on other sites in other cities, it's a stolen-photo scam. Budget for Naples's €5/night tourism tax on rooms >€120/night; refuse any 'city fee in cash on arrival' without a receipt and legal justification.
scams.location: Apartment listings in the Centro Storico, Chiaia, Vomero, Sanità, and near Napoli Centrale; also outlying Ischia, Sorrento Peninsula, and Cilento listings sold as 'Naples base'
